cards.explanation: The one at the door is her beloved, knocking. She says, "A sound! My beloved is knocking…" (Song of Solomon 5:2). Then he speaks up himself: "Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one." A knock at night, and he really wants in.

The word is open. He says, "Open to me…" and then tells her his head is drenched with dew and his hair with the dampness of the night (Song of Solomon 5:2). I think a man dripping like that wants that door open, and fast, friends. I'd be knocking with my whole mustache.

She wonders if she must put her robe back on. She says she has taken off her robe and asks, "…must I put it back on?" Then she adds that she's washed her feet and asks, "…must I soil them again?" (Song of Solomon 5:3). A knock came right when she'd settled in, and I'd be standing there in the dark wondering the same thing.

The word is heart. "My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him." (Song of Solomon 5:4). Back in verse 2 she said her heart was awake while she slept. That heart does not sit still when he's close, friends.

The answer is False. She says, "I rose up to open for my beloved." and then, "I opened for my beloved…" (Song of Solomon 5:5-6). She asked questions about her robe and her feet, but then she rose. Those questions didn't keep her from the door.

When she opens the door, she finds he has turned and gone. She says, "I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone." Then comes, "My heart sank at his departure." (Song of Solomon 5:6). She did get up and open the door, and he wasn't there. I think that's a hard moment, and it's okay to feel it.

The answer is True. She says, "I sought him but did not find him. I called, but he did not answer." (Song of Solomon 5:6). She's looking and she's calling, and all she gets back is quiet. I think that quiet is the heaviest part of this verse.

She wants them to tell him that she is sick with love. Her words are, "…if you find my beloved, tell him I am sick with love." (Song of Solomon 5:8). She's just been beaten and lost her cloak, but that's not what she sends. She sends what's in her heart. It's a short message, friends, and I think it says everything.

The word is beautiful. They ask, "How is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful among women?" (Song of Solomon 5:9). They call her that again in 6:1. Same title, both times they speak to her.

She paints a picture of what he's like. From verse 10 through 16 she describes him from his head down: purest gold, hair black as a raven, eyes like doves, lips like lilies. She doesn't give a short answer, friends. She gives them the whole portrait.

She's saying no one else compares to him. Ten thousand is a big crowd, and she calls him "…outstanding among ten thousand." (Song of Solomon 5:10). She picks him out of all of them. In her eyes, nobody stands next to him.

The answer is False. She starts at the top with "His head is purest gold…" (Song of Solomon 5:11). Then come his eyes, cheeks, lips, arms and body, and his legs in verse 15. She keeps going after that to his mouth in verse 16, so it's head first.

She's saying he is her companion as well as her love. She says, "This is my beloved, and this is my friend…" (Song of Solomon 5:16). He isn't one or the other. He's both her love and her friend, and I think that's a good thing to have in one person.
The word is seek, friends. The daughters of Jerusalem say, "We will seek him with you." (Song of Solomon 6:1). Earlier she "…sought him but did not find him." Now they offer to seek him with her.

She tells them where he has gone. "My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies." (Song of Solomon 6:2). Back in 5:6 she sought him and did not find him, and when she called, he did not answer. Now the daughters ask where he has gone, and she knows exactly where to point. That's a woman who went from searching to knowing.

The answer is True. She says, "I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me…" (Song of Solomon 6:3). That comes after the empty doorway and her search. I think it's a strong thing to say after that, friends.
